programme.title: How Do They Do It S13 - "Cameras/Big Airbags/ Jelly Beans"
programme.desc: How do they take the world’s sharpest photos? How do they stitch an airbag that can catch a falling car? How do they make billions of perfect jelly beans?

programme.title: Speed S1 - "Across Oceans"
programme.desc: Throughout history, human society has run on trade. The innovations that allowed faster and more accurate oceanic travel revolutionized the world. New inventions now help people and goods move on the water faster for recreation and commerce.

programme.title: Speed S1 - "Across Continents"
programme.desc: Never in the history of humanity have so many of us been mobile. New innovations propel us into the world of self-driving cars and high-speed trains.

programme.title: Speed S1 - "Into the Skies"
programme.desc: Growth in air transportation is set to soar, carrying over 10 billion passengers every year by 2050. To cope requires us to radically rethink aircraft design. Join us as we look into the world's most innovative research and development labs.

programme.title: Science of Thrills S1 - "Height"
programme.desc: Engineer and adventurer Rob Bell climbs aboard four spectacular rollercoasters in Europe and America that exploit our fear of heights.

programme.title: Speed S1 - "Into Space"
programme.desc: The most innovative area of human motion lies not on Earth, but with the exploration of space. Meet the private space entrepreneurs jostling to offer the tantalizing prospect of cheap, frequent travel beyond the atmosphere into Earth orbit.

programme.title: Life of Cards S1 - "Daniel Negreanu"
programme.desc: The most profitable poker player of all time, Daniel Negreanu, tries to stay on top of his game and give back to the country that brought him fame and fortune.

programme.title: Life of Cards S1 - "Chris Moneymaker"
programme.desc: Road trip with all-American family man and anti-hero Chris Moneymaker who became a poker celebrity overnight and gives a new meaning to stardom.

programme.title: Hollywood Weapons: Fact or Fiction? S2 - "Terry Down Under"
programme.desc: Terry and Larry start off the new season testing one of the most requested films, Quigley Down Under. Terry will see if he can hit a 564-yard shot with a Sharps rifle. An 800-yard shot, trying to kill 2 bad guys with 1 bullet!

programme.title: Hollywood Weapons: Fact or Fiction? S2 - "Bond, Terry Bond"
programme.desc: Terry and Larry will be testing the effectiveness of driving a vehicle with fully automatic machine guns mounted to the car! Just like 007 did with his Aston Martin DB5.

programme.title: Hollywood Weapons: Fact or Fiction? S2 - "Just-Terry-Fied"
programme.desc: Terry and Larry will be test 2 scenes from Justified where, Terry, aka Raylan Givins finds himself in a bathtub and a dead body lying over top of him.

programme.title: Hollywood Weapons: Fact or Fiction? S2 - "Terry's Reindeer Game"
programme.desc: Terry and Larry test a scene from Reindeer Games when Ben Affleck and Charlize Theron get trapped under a frozen lake, and they escape by shooting 3 shots with a 12-gauge shot gun underwater to blast a hole in the ice to escape.

programme.title: VR 101 S1 - "Medicine"
programme.desc: From physical examination, and surgery to Psychotherapy and Autism treatment. Even Traditional Chinese medicine can be practiced on VR.

programme.title: VR 101 S1 - "Future of VR"
programme.desc: In this episode, we make some virtual friends, have some virtual meetings, do some virtual research.

programme.title: Survival Science S1 - "Surviving a Bear Attack"
programme.desc: Nick and Laura create kick-ass tests to explore the immense power and startling speed of grizzly bears. They use Hollywood stunt tools to experience an attack. Then try to recreate a “miracle” arrow shot that saved a man from being killed by a bear.

programme.title: Survival Science S1 - "Surviving Treestand Accidents"
programme.desc: In this exciting episode we’ll find out the reasons why tree stand accidents happen and how we can prevent them. Cool science mixed with dynamic experiments send our hosts, our stunt team and our special crash test dummies plummeting to the ground.

programme.title: Survival Science S1 - "Sniper Attack"
programme.desc: Military snipers are trained in a variety of skills: detection, stalking, camouflage, infiltration, special reconnaissance and target acquisition. Bottom line, a ton of cool shooting and science for Nick and Laura to explore!

programme.title: Survival Science S1 - "Surviving a Lightning Strike"
programme.desc: Laura and Nick travel to a state-of-the-art Direct Effects Lightning Test Lab. With some “explosive” experiments, they’ll determine the power lightning and how it behaves? And they’ll find out how can hunters and fishermen best protect themselves?

programme.title: Bright Now S1 - "Ketamine: From Street Drug to Lifesaver"
programme.sub-title: Ketamine: From Street Drug to Lifesaver
programme.desc: Worldwide, depression afflicts more than 300 million people, making it the leading global cause of disability. Suicide is the 2nd leading cause of death in the world for those aged 15-24 years. Now there may be a new tool in fighting that depression.

programme.title: The World of Bridges S1 - "China"
programme.desc: We visit China's most famous Wind and Rain Bridge and the Ponte dei Salti in the Verzasca Valley that literally dates back to the Roman era.

programme.title: The World of Bridges S1 - "Wales"
programme.desc: The Millau Viaduct in the south of France is one of the highest bridge structures in the world while the Pontcysyllte Aqueduct, which stands high over the River Dee in northeast Wales, was built in the 19th century.

programme.title: The World of Bridges S1 - "India"
programme.desc: One of the most impressive steel bridges in the world can be found in Calcutta: the Howrah Bridge. Its predecessor is the Forth Bridge across the Firth of Forth, near the Scottish capital of Edinburgh.

programme.title: The World of Bridges S1 - "Zimbabwe"
programme.desc: The Great Seto Bridge in Japan and the Victoria Falls Bridge in Zimbabwe have more than one thing in common: they were built on dreams and are the only train connections between the two regions.

programme.title: Ancient Engineering S1 - "Secrets Of Notre Dame"
programme.desc: Building for God reached a high point in the Middle Ages when a new engineering movement emerged in Europe, changing the rules forever.

programme.title: Ancient Engineering S1 - "Secrets Of Angkor Wat"
programme.desc: Temples, designed to honor the Gods, have been at the heart of cities since the earliest times

programme.title: Ancient Engineering S1 - "The Power Of Water"
programme.desc: Without water, civilization is simply not possible. Romans took control of their water supplies very, very seriously.

programme.title: Ancient Engineering S1 - "History’s Greatest Ships"
programme.desc: As far back as the Bronze Age, humans were building ships capable of crossing oceans and trading between continents.

programme.title: Trajectory S1 - "Mercury Advances"
programme.desc: PROJECT MERCURY ADVANCES - America’s first manned space program finally puts a man in orbit. CAMERA TRACKING - The array of special cameras that follow a spacecraft at launch.

programme.title: Trajectory S1 - "Venus Express"
programme.desc: PROJECT GEMINI COMMENCES - Did Gemini give the US a lead in the space race? VENUS EXPRESS - The last days of ESA’s Venus probe. EMU NASA’s - Extravehicular Mobility Unit. DEEP SPACE COMMUNICATIONS - ESA’s worldwide network of giant dishes.

programme.title: Trajectory S1 - "More about Mars"
programme.desc: PROJECT GEMINI ADVANCES - NASA refines the techniques needed for rendezvous. CASSINI AT SATURN - In the Cassini probe’s final years of activity, its handlers are asking it to do more complex and risky assignments.

programme.title: Trajectory S1 - "Swarm"
programme.desc: PROJECT GEMINI DOCKING AND EVA - In the final phase of the Gemini program NASA struggles with docking and spacewalks. CURIOUSITY ROVING MARS - On the surface of Mars the Curiousity rover is changing the way we think about the red planet.

programme.title: The Lightbulb Moment S1 - "INTERSTATE"
programme.desc: Dwight Eisenhower’s interstate highway system was the biggest infrastructure project of its time, a bold plan to connect all corners of America and boost the economy. So how did it end up deepening the divide between rich and poor?

programme.title: The Lightbulb Moment S1 - "EDISON"
programme.desc: Edison pioneered the world’s first research and development center in Menlo Park, New Jersey, working with a group of experimenters to methodically zero in on the holy grail of electric light.

programme.desc: How do they make baklava, the favourite sweet of the Ottomans? How do they fly a gyroplane, James Bond’s vehicle of choice? How do they craft a ukulele, the Hawaiian instrument played by Elvis? How do they build a supercat, the world’s fastest ferry?

programme.desc: How do they carve longboards, the skateboard’s bigger, faster brother? How do they turn tonnes of lemons into millions of bottles of lemons? How do they build industry’s versatile heavy lifter, the forklift truck?
